story.head: Carrick meets his old team
paras: The Rangers (13-9-1) lost 5-2 to Carolina on Sunday, while the Sabres (10-10-4) beat Tampa Bay 6-2 the same night. Going in, the Rangers are third in the Metropolitan (tied for 16th in the NHL) and the Sabres sixth in the Atlantic (tied for 19th).
This season, the Sabres have been outscored 82-73, but they’re even at 50-50 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 25-14.

The Rangers get more of their shots from in close than almost anyone (2nd), hit a lot (2nd) and get a lot of their shots blocked (32nd). As for the Sabres, they rarely get pinned in their own end (3rd) and get their defensemen shooting (5th), but don’t block many shots (30th). The Sabres’ good looks will be harder to come by against the Rangers, and the Rangers’ power play (8th) could do real damage against the Sabres’ penalty kill (24th).

Adam Fox (2 G / 24 A / 26 P in 23 GP) leads the Rangers in scoring, and Alexis Lafrenière (10 G / 12 A / 22 P in 23 GP) has a team-high ten goals. For the Sabres, Tage Thompson (17 G / 11 A / 28 P in 24 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Jack Quinn (13 G / 11 A / 24 P in 24 GP) isn’t far behind.
Joonas Korpisalo (3-0-0 / .940 SV% in 3 GS) is expected to start for the Rangers, and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen (7-4-3 / .878 SV% in 13 GS) for Buffalo.
